home.title: Medind – Pill Reminder & Medication Tracker for iPhone
home.description: Medind is a simple pill reminder app for iPhone. Reminders ring like an alarm, even on silent. Tap Taken and see what you took and when. No account, data stays on your phone.
home.h1: The pill reminder that rings until you take it
home.lead: Medind is a simple medication reminder app for iPhone. It rings like an alarm, even when your phone is on silent, and keeps a clear record of every dose you take.
home.body:
Everything you need, nothing you don't

  • Rings like an alarm

    Reminders ring through silent mode and Focus, with a big Taken button and snooze. You will hear it.

  • Did I take it? One look

    The Today screen shows each dose with the time you took it. The calendar shows every day before.

  • Your medication, your words

    Type the name you use and add a photo of the pill or box, so you always know which one is which.

  • Any schedule

    Times each day, chosen weekdays, every few days, every few hours, or only when needed.

  • Big, clear and calm

    Large text, large buttons, plain words. Made so anyone can use it without help.

  • Private by design

    No account and no ads. Everything you enter stays on your iPhone.

Set up in three steps

  1. Add a medication. Type its name and take a photo if you like.
  2. Choose when. Pick the times and days, or every few hours.
  3. Tap Taken when it rings. Medind saves the time, so you never have to remember.

Also included

  • A home screen and lock screen widget with a Taken button
  • Measurements such as blood pressure, pulse and weight, saved as you type them
  • Steps and other values from Apple Health, shown live and never saved
  • Export and backup of everything you entered
  • 18 languages

If you stop paying, your reminders keep ringing

Medind is a subscription with a clear price shown in the App Store before you pay. Reminders you have already set keep working even if your subscription ends. Medication reminders are too important to switch off.
faq: Does Medind ring when my iPhone is on silent?
Yes. Medind uses Apple's alarm system for iOS 26, so reminders ring through silent mode and Focus, just like the Clock app's alarms.
Is Medind good for older adults?
Yes. It was made for people over 60: large text, large buttons, plain words and one main action on each screen.
Do I need an account?
No. There is no sign-up and no login. Everything you enter stays on your iPhone.
Does Medind give medical advice?
No. Medind never tells you what or how much to take. It reminds you at the times you choose and records what you mark as taken.
Can I track medication that I take only when needed?
Yes. Add it as “when needed” and tap Taken each time you take it. Medind saves the time.
What does Medind cost?
Medind is a subscription. The price for your country is shown in the App Store and in the app before you pay, and you can restore your purchase at any time.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy – Medind
privacy.description: How Medind handles your data: no account, no ads, no tracking. Your medication data stays on your iPhone.
privacy.lead: Short version: everything you enter stays on your iPhone. We have no account system, no ads and no analytics, and we never see your medication or health data.
privacy.body:
What Medind stores

Your medications, photos, schedules, the doses you mark as taken, notes and measurements are stored only on your iPhone, inside the app. The widget reads the same data on the same phone. We do not have a server that receives this data.

Apple Health

If you allow it, Medind reads steps, pulse, weight and blood pressure from Apple Health to show them in the app. These values are read live and are never saved by Medind, never included in backups and never sent anywhere. Medind does not write anything to Apple Health.

Camera and photos

If you take a photo of a medication, the photo is stored on your iPhone only.

Purchases

Payments are handled by Apple. To check whether your subscription is active, Medind uses RevenueCat, a subscription service. RevenueCat receives an anonymous app ID and purchase information such as which subscription you bought and when. It never receives your medication, measurement or health data. See RevenueCat's privacy policy.

No tracking, no ads, no analytics

Medind contains no advertising, no tracking and no analytics. We do not sell or share your data.

Backups and exports

You can export your data or make a backup file from the app. That file is created on your phone and goes only where you choose to send or save it. If you use iPhone backup (iCloud or computer), Apple may include the app's data in that backup, as for any app; this is controlled by you in your iPhone settings.

Reminders

Reminders and alarms are scheduled on your iPhone. They do not go through any server.

Deleting your data

Delete the app to delete all data stored by Medind on your iPhone. Because we never receive your medication data, there is nothing for us to delete on our side.

Children

Medind is not directed at children under 13.

This website

This website uses no cookies and no tracking. The free tools on this site run in your browser; what you type into them is not sent anywhere.

Changes

If this policy changes, we will update this page and the date below.

Contact

Questions about privacy: {EMAIL}

support.title: Support – Medind Pill Reminder
support.description: Get help with Medind: reminders, purchases, backups and more. Email us and we will reply as soon as we can.
support.lead: Need help or have an idea? Email us. A real person reads every message.
support.body:
Email {EMAIL}

Please tell us your iPhone model and what you expected to happen. A screenshot helps a lot.
faq: My reminder did not ring. What should I do?

Open Medind and go to Settings. Under Reminders you can see whether Medind is allowed to ring, turn reminders on, and tap Test reminder to hear one. If reminders are off, tap Open Settings and allow alarms and notifications for Medind.
How do I restore my purchase on a new iPhone?
Sign in with the same Apple Account, open Medind, go to Settings and tap Restore purchase.
How do I cancel my subscription?
Subscriptions are managed by Apple. Open the Settings app on your iPhone, tap your name, then Subscriptions, and choose Medind. Your reminders keep ringing after you cancel.
How do I move my data to a new iPhone?

In Medind's Settings, tap Save a backup and keep the file, for example in iCloud Drive or email it to yourself. On the new iPhone, open Settings in Medind and tap Restore a backup. You can also restore your whole iPhone from an iCloud or computer backup.
How do I export my history or measurements?
In Medind's Settings, tap Export my data. You get a file you can share with your doctor or save.
Which languages does Medind support?
English, Arabic, Chinese (Traditional), Dutch, Finnish, French, German, Hungarian, Italian, Japanese, Korean, Polish, Portuguese, Russian, Spanish, Thai, Turkish and Vietnamese.
Does Medind work on Android or Apple Watch?
Not yet. Medind is for iPhone with iOS 26 or later.

dose_calculator.title: Dose Time Calculator – Every 4, 6, 8 or 12 Hours Schedule
dose_calculator.description: Free dose time calculator: enter your first dose time and how many hours apart, and get every dose time for the day. Works for every 4, 6, 8 or 12 hours.
dose_calculator.lead: Enter the time of your first dose and how many hours apart your doses are. You get the clock time of every dose in a day.
dose_calculator.body:
This tool only does the clock math. Always take your medication the way your doctor, pharmacist or the package leaflet says.

How it works

A day has 24 hours. If you take a medication every 8 hours, that is 3 doses a day: for example 8:00, 16:00 and 0:00. Every 6 hours is 4 doses, every 4 hours is 6 doses and every 12 hours is 2 doses.

Tips for doses through the night

  • Choose a first dose time that puts the night dose when you are usually awake, if your instructions allow it.
  • Ask your pharmacist whether the times can move a little to fit your sleep.
  • Use an alarm that rings even when the phone is on silent, so a night dose is not missed.

Medind can remind you every few hours automatically and rings even on silent.
faq: What times are every 8 hours?
If your first dose is at 8:00, every 8 hours is 8:00, 16:00 and 0:00 (midnight). If your first dose is at 7:00, it is 7:00, 15:00 and 23:00.
What times are every 6 hours?
Starting at 6:00, every 6 hours is 6:00, 12:00, 18:00 and 0:00.
What does twice a day mean?
Often it means about every 12 hours, for example 8:00 and 20:00. Check your leaflet or ask your pharmacist, because some medications have their own rules.

schedule_maker.title: Free Printable Medication Schedule Maker (Pill Chart)
schedule_maker.description: Make a printable medication schedule in one minute. Add each medication and its times, then print a weekly pill chart with check boxes. Free and private.
schedule_maker.lead: Add your medications and times, then print a weekly chart with a box to tick for every dose. Good for the fridge, a care home or a family member who helps.
schedule_maker.body:
How to use the chart

  1. Write each medication the way it says on the box, so anyone can find the right one.
  2. Add one time for each dose. A medication you take morning and evening gets two times.
  3. Print it and tick the box each time you take a dose.

Prefer your phone? Medind does this for you, rings at each time and saves the time you tapped Taken.
faq: What should a medication schedule include?
The name of each medication as written on the box, the strength if you have more than one, and the time of each dose. A tick box for each day helps you see what you have taken.
Is my information saved?
No. The chart is made in your browser. Nothing you type is sent or stored.

guides.title: Medication Reminder Guides – Tips to Never Miss a Dose
guides.description: Plain guides about remembering your medication: daily habits, setting medication reminders on iPhone and helping an older parent.
guides.lead: Practical guides for remembering medication, for yourself or someone you care for.

guide_remember.title: How to Remember to Take Your Medication: 12 Simple Tips
guide_remember.description: 12 practical tips to remember your medication every day: link it to a routine, use a pillbox, set alarms that ring on silent and keep a simple record.
guide_remember.h1: How to remember to take your medication: 12 simple tips
guide_remember.lead: Forgetting a dose is very common, and it is not about being careless. These tips help you build a routine that works on busy days too.
guide_remember.body:
1. Link it to something you already do

Take your medication right after something you do every day without thinking: brushing your teeth, your first coffee or breakfast. The old habit reminds you of the new one.

2. Keep it where you will see it

Put the medication next to your toothbrush or the coffee maker, if it may be stored there. Out of sight is out of mind. Keep it away from children and out of humid bathrooms when the label says so.

3. Use a weekly pillbox

A pillbox with one compartment per day shows at a glance whether today's dose is gone. Fill it on the same day each week.

4. Set a reminder that you cannot miss

A normal notification is easy to swipe away or miss when the phone is on silent. Use a reminder that rings like an alarm until you confirm it.

5. Record each dose when you take it

The question “did I already take it?” is the main reason people double up or skip. Tick it off on paper or tap Taken in an app the moment you take it.

6. Know each medication by sight

Take a photo of each pill and box. When a pharmacy switches brands, the pill may look different, so update the photo.

7. Use one time zone plan for travel

Before you travel, ask your pharmacist how to shift your times. Then set your reminders for the new times.

8. Pack a spare day

Keep one day's medication in your bag or car for days when you are not home on time.

9. Make a printed schedule

A printed chart on the fridge helps everyone in the house. Use our free medication schedule maker.

10. Plan for doses every few hours

If you take a medication every 6 or 8 hours, write out the clock times. The dose time calculator does the math.

11. Ask for help when it gets complicated

If you take many medications, ask your pharmacist for a medication review. They can often simplify the times.

12. Be kind to yourself

If you miss a dose, check the package leaflet or ask your pharmacist what to do. Do not double the next dose unless you are told to.
faq: What is the easiest way to remember to take pills?
Link the dose to a daily habit, keep the medication where you see it, and use a reminder that rings until you confirm it.
What should I do if I forgot a dose?
Read the package leaflet or ask your pharmacist. The answer is different for each medication.

guide_iphone.title: How to Set Medication Reminders on iPhone (That Ring on Silent)
guide_iphone.description: Step-by-step: set medication reminders on iPhone with the Health app or an app like Medind, and make sure they ring when your iPhone is on silent.
guide_iphone.h1: How to set medication reminders on iPhone
guide_iphone.lead: Your iPhone can remind you to take your medication in a few ways. Here is how each one works, and how to make sure the reminder is not silenced.
guide_iphone.body:
Option 1: The Health app

  1. Open the Health app and tap Browse (or Search), then Medications.
  2. Tap Add Medication and follow the steps to enter the name, type and schedule.
  3. To be reminded again if you forget, scroll down to Options and turn on Follow Up Reminders.
  4. To hear reminders when the iPhone is muted or in a Focus, tap Critical Alerts in Options and turn them on for your medications.

The Health app is free and built in. Reminders arrive as notifications.

Option 2: A pill reminder app that rings like an alarm

Medind uses Apple's alarm system on iOS 26. A reminder fills the screen and rings like the Clock app's alarm, with a large Taken button and snooze. It rings through silent mode and Focus.

  1. Install Medind and add your medication by name, with a photo if you like.
  2. Choose the times, days or every few hours.
  3. Allow alarms when Medind asks.
  4. When it rings, tap Taken. Medind saves the time.

Option 3: Clock app alarms

You can set an ordinary alarm in the Clock app and name it after your medication. It rings on silent, but it does not keep a record of what you took.

Why do reminders not ring on silent?

Normal notifications follow the ring/silent switch and Focus. Only alarms and critical alerts break through. If you rely on reminders, use one of those.

Check your reminders work

  • Set a test reminder two minutes from now and put the phone on silent.
  • In iPhone Settings, check that notifications and alarms are allowed for the app you use.
  • Check the volume in Settings › Sounds, because alarms use the ringer volume.
faq: Can iPhone remind me to take medication?
Yes. The Health app has medication reminders, and apps like Medind can ring like an alarm at each dose time.
How do I make medication reminders ring on silent?
Turn on Critical Alerts for medications in the Health app, or use an app that uses iPhone alarms, such as Medind on iOS 26.

guide_elderly.title: Medication Reminders for Elderly Parents: A Practical Guide
guide_elderly.description: How to help an elderly parent remember their medication without taking over: simple routines, reminders that ring, printed charts and respectful check-ins.
guide_elderly.lead: Helping a parent with medication works best when they stay in charge. These steps keep things simple and respectful.
guide_elderly.body:
Start with a conversation

Ask what is hard: remembering, telling pills apart, or knowing whether a dose was taken. The answer tells you what to fix. Let your parent choose what helps.

Make the medications easy to tell apart

Write the name in large letters on each box, or take a photo of each pill. When the pharmacy changes the brand, look together at the new pill.

Choose reminders they can hear

Many older adults keep their phone on silent by accident. A reminder that rings like an alarm, with one big button, is easier than a small notification. Medind was designed for this: large text, plain words and a Taken button.

Make “did I take it?” easy to answer

Doubt leads to skipped or double doses. A pillbox or an app that records the time of each dose answers the question in one look.

Put a printed schedule on the fridge

A paper chart helps visitors and carers too. Make one with the free medication schedule maker.

Check in without taking over

A short call at the same time each week to look at the week together works better than daily checks. Celebrate a good week.

Ask the pharmacist

Ask for a medication review if your parent takes many medicines. Pharmacists can often simplify times or suggest blister packs.
faq: What is the best medication reminder for an elderly person?
One they can hear and understand: a reminder that rings like an alarm, with large text and one clear button, plus a way to see what has been taken.
How can I make sure my parent took their medication?
Use a pillbox you can look at together, or an app that records the time of each dose. Agree on this with your parent so they stay in charge.
